title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI
talk_summary: The talk reports experiments on an AI tutor showing that default compaction/summarization often hurts because it breaks prompt caching and drops details; keeping full history with caching was cheaper, faster, and higher recall in their tests. It also covers hybrid retrieval, progressive disclosure, logging, and cheaper-model routing, with the main lesson to measure context policies against real tasks before adopting them.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep full conversation history and rely on provider prompt caching instead of routinely summarizing or compacting context, because transformed context loses cache hits.
takeaways.numbers: Full history cheapest/fastest/best recall; 97% cached tokens; DeepSeek cache up to 50x cheaper; summarization recall 32% vs 95%.

takeaways.what_they_do: They run multiple context presets on real student questions and multi-turn recall probes, logging tokens, cached tokens, cost, TTFT, tool calls, and whether compaction fired.
takeaways.numbers: 11 presets; ~$500-600 eval run; 60 single-turn pairs; 11-13 turn sessions.

takeaways.what_they_do: They found clearing old tool outputs forces the agent to re-call tools for information it already had, increasing cost/latency and reducing recall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you remove the tool outputs consistently then the agent needs to rerieve uh afterwards for information it already had
takeaways.numbers: Production multi-turn quality degraded to 38%; full history cheaper/faster/better recall.

takeaways.what_they_do: They use hybrid semantic+BM25 retrieval, rerank top chunks, and maintain a small wiki/index with pointers so the agent loads only relevant context progressively.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're actually using a hybrid search we're using a mix of both
takeaways.numbers: 8M-token corpus; top 30 chunks reranked to top 5; dense RAG 0% at 400k vs BM25 100%; local doc RAG 100% accuracy.

takeaways.technique: Cheaper cache-friendly model for high-volume context
takeaways.what_they_do: They route high-volume tutor traffic to a cheaper model with strong prompt caching, keeping full history, after evals showed similar quality at much lower cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cheaper model is u what brought the cost down but the results are the same
takeaways.numbers: Gemini ~$40k/mo vs DeepSeek ~$1.9k/mo at 1,000 students; DeepSeek cache 50x; 97% cached.

takeaways.what_they_do: They split capabilities into small precise skills that reference each other and load only the skill needed for the current task or subagent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everyone is is converging towards having more and smaller skills
